steps.title: The Opening Question
steps.content:
So {{contact_first_name}}, how have things been going since you had your teeth whitening done with us? Is your smile still looking bright and white and you're loving it, has a little staining started to creep back, or are you pretty much back to where you were before you started with us?

(This question has only three possible answers. Click the one you hear.)

steps.title: Still Bright: Celebrate the Win
steps.content:
I love hearing that, {{contact_first_name}}. That’s exactly what we want. There’s nothing like catching your smile in a photo and actually loving it.

Do you remember how much it bothered you before? Holding back in pictures, noticing it every time you looked in the mirror? (Let them enjoy the moment. This is their win.)

(Do not pitch anything yet. The file update comes next, and the close follows if nothing else surfaces.)

steps.title: Starting to Dull: Normalize, Then Update the File
steps.content:
{{contact_first_name}}, that is completely normal, honestly, you’re right on track. Everyday life re-stains teeth for everyone: the morning coffee, the tea, the glass of wine with dinner. It has nothing to do with the whitening not working. It worked beautifully. It’s just that life keeps happening to your teeth.

I remember how much you loved your results when you were in. (Let them respond. Be warm, no alarm. This is routine, not a problem.)

(Do not pitch anything yet. The file update comes next, and the close follows if nothing else surfaces.)

steps.title: Back to Where It Was: Warm Empathy, Then Update the File
steps.content:
{{contact_first_name}}, I completely understand. Staining is cumulative: every coffee, every tea, every glass of wine adds a little, and after enough time it settles back in. It’s completely normal, and it is very easy to fix.

I remember how great your smile looked and how happy you were when you saw the results. (Let them respond. Be warm. If they express frustration about it coming back, reassure: that’s just how teeth work for everyone, and it has nothing to do with anything they did wrong.)

(Do not pitch anything yet. The file update comes next, and the close follows if nothing else surfaces.)

steps.title: One More Thing: The Sensitivity Question
steps.content:
Perfect, you’re all set for (day) at (time).

(If you already covered sensitivity during the file update, skip the question, just confirm the appointment warmly and end the call, noting any sensitivity on their file.)

Oh, one quick thing while I have you, {{contact_first_name}}, because it makes a real difference in how comfortable your visit is: have you noticed any sensitivity to hot or cold, with your coffee, ice water, that kind of thing?

If YES: I’m really glad you told me. That’s super common, and there’s a lot we can do about it. We’ll plan your visit around it: a desensitizing treatment beforehand makes the whole experience much more comfortable. I’ll make a note on your file so {{rec_pronoun}} can take care of that when you’re in.

If NO: Perfect, that makes everything easy. We’ll see you (day) at (time), {{contact_first_name}}. We can’t wait to see that smile!

(Either way, the call ends warm, with the appointment confirmed.)

steps.title: The Transition: Update the File
steps.content:
Now {{contact_first_name}}, while I have you on the phone, I’d like to ask you a few quick questions so we get your file completely up to date. Is that okay?

(Wait for the yes before starting the questions.)

steps.title: The Transition: Update the File
steps.content:
Now {{contact_first_name}}, while I have you on the phone, I’d like to ask you a few quick questions so we get your file completely up to date. Is that okay?

(Wait for the yes before starting the questions.)

steps.title: The Six Questions: Update the File
steps.content:
(Ask these in order. Critical: write down everything they mention. You’ll read it back before the recommendation. Never give dental advice on the call.)

Now, you mentioned your smile is still looking bright. I love hearing that. One thing I’ll ask, just because staining is so sneaky: is it still as bright as day one, or have you noticed even a shade of dulling, maybe in certain light or in photos?

How about the daily stainers? Coffee, tea, red wine? Still enjoying them the same as always? (No judgment. We just note it on the file so we know what your smile is up against.)

Have you noticed any sensitivity to hot or cold, with your coffee, ice water, that kind of thing?

Beyond the brightness, is there anything else about your smile you’ve ever wondered about or wished were different? Anything you’d want a professional’s opinion on?

Anything coming up on the calendar, a wedding, a reunion, photos, a big interview, that you’d want your smile camera-ready for?

Last one, and it’s my favorite. If you could wave a wand and change just one thing about your smile, no judgment, what would it be?

(If they mentioned anything at all, read it back and click the first button. If truly nothing surfaced, fall through to the stay-ahead close. That’s still a great call.)

steps.title: The Six Questions: Update the File
steps.content:
(Ask these in order. Critical: write down everything they mention. You’ll read it back before the recommendation. Never give dental advice on the call.)

You mentioned some staining has come back. When did you start noticing it, and is it everywhere or mostly in certain spots?

How about the daily stainers? Coffee, tea, red wine? Still enjoying them the same as always? (No judgment. We just note it on the file so we know what your smile is up against.)

Have you noticed any sensitivity to hot or cold, with your coffee, ice water, that kind of thing?

Beyond the brightness, is there anything else about your smile you’ve ever wondered about or wished were different? Anything you’d want a professional’s opinion on?

Anything coming up on the calendar, a wedding, a reunion, photos, a big interview, that you’d want your smile camera-ready for?

Last one, and it’s my favorite. If you could wave a wand and change just one thing about your smile, no judgment, what would it be?

(If they mentioned anything beyond the staining itself, read it back and click the first button. If getting the brightness back is the whole story, fall through to the close.)

steps.title: The Review & Bridge to Emotion
steps.content:
{{contact_first_name}}, let me make sure I've got this right. (Recap what they told you: how long it's been on your mind, how often you notice it, and how it's been affecting them.) Did I get that right?

And it sounds like what you'd really love is to feel good every time you catch your reflection, not to think twice about it, is that fair to say?

(Forward-looking, warm, never shaming. About 95% say yes. That yes is the moment.)

steps.title: Making It Real
steps.content:
(Take the concern they named and make it present with three questions, in order. Write down their answers. You’ll use them in the next section.)

How long has that been on your mind? Just recently, a few months, or has it been bugging you for a while now?

How often do you notice it? Every time you look in the mirror, every photo, or just now and then?

And the last thing I’d like to ask is how it affects you. When you notice it, what does it do? Do you hold back in photos, cover your smile, think about it in conversations? (Let them open up. Do not rush.)

Then respond with empathy: Thank you for sharing that. It makes complete sense, and that is exactly the kind of thing {{rec_pronoun}} help people with every single day.

steps.title: They Hesitate: Uncover Why
steps.content:
{{contact_first_name}}, help me understand. What's holding you back from coming in to take a look? Is it the timing, or is there something else on your mind?

(Ask this easygoing and curious, not pushy. You're simply trying to understand what's getting in the way so you can help. Then stop and let them tell you.)

What are your thoughts about that?

steps.title: The Magic Question & Recommendation
steps.content:
{{contact_first_name}}, it sounds like it might be worth having {{rec_obj}} take a look at that. Can I make a recommendation?

(Wait for yes.)

My recommendation is that we get you back in so {{rec_pronoun}} can take a look at what you just told me about and see if there’s something {{rec_pronoun}} can do to take care of it for you. And I’ll tell you the same thing I tell everyone: if {{rec_pronoun}} think there’s something {{rec_pronoun}} can do to help you, {{rec_pronoun}}’ll let you know, and {{rec_pronoun}}’d be honored if you let {{rec_obj}}. And if for some reason {{rec_pronoun}} don’t think it’s the right fit, {{rec_pronoun}}’ll tell you that too, because the last thing {{rec_pronoun}} want to do is waste your time or your money. Does that sound reasonable?

(Ask “does that sound reasonable”, never “does that sound good.” Click what you hear next.)

steps.title: Nothing Surfaced: Stay Ahead of It Close
steps.content:
{{contact_first_name}}, I’m really glad your smile is still looking bright. That’s exactly what we like to hear.

Now, there is one thing I want to mention before I let you go. Here’s the sneaky thing about staining. It creeps back so gradually you never see it happening. The coffee, the tea, the red wine. Day by day it dulls things just a shade at a time, and because you see your own smile every day, you’re always the last one to notice. Usually the first time people realize it is that moment of looking at a photo and wondering where the brightness went. Does that make sense?

(Wait for the yes. If they hesitate, use the button below to uncover the real concern.)

{{contact_first_name}}, can I make a recommendation? (Wait for the yes.)

My recommendation is we get you in for a quick touch-up. That way you stay ahead of the staining instead of chasing it. Does that sound reasonable?

(Wait for the yes.)

Okay, let’s find you a time. I have (day) at (time) or (day) at (time). Which is better for you?

steps.title: Getting the Brightness Back Is the Story: The Close
steps.content:
{{contact_first_name}}, here’s something most people don’t realize: the whitening you did before is still working for you underneath. What’s settled in since is newer surface stain sitting on top of it, and newer stain lifts a lot easier than years of buildup. So getting your brightness back is a much smaller job than it was the first time around. Does that make sense?

(Wait for the yes.)

{{contact_first_name}}, can I make a recommendation? (Wait for the yes.)

My recommendation is we get you in for that touch-up now. Getting back to that bright smile you loved is a single visit away. Does that sound reasonable?

(Wait for the yes.)

Okay, let’s get you back on the books. I have (day) at (time) or (day) at (time). Which is better for you?

steps.title: Objection: I thought it would last longer
steps.content:
I completely understand, and that's a great point. Whitening looks amazing but teeth naturally restain over time with coffee, wine, and everyday foods. That's exactly why coming in makes sense, so {{rec_pronoun}} can take a look and talk through the best way to get your smile bright again and help it last.

Confirm and continue: Does that make sense? (Wait for a fast yes.) Do you have any other questions or concerns?

steps.title: Objection: I’m embarrassed it stained back up
steps.content:
Please don't be. Staining is cumulative; every coffee, tea, and glass of wine adds a little over time, and it's exactly why we reach out, with no judgment at all. {{rec_pronoun_cap}}'d simply love to help you get your smile back to where it was.

Confirm and continue: Does that make sense? (Wait for a fast yes.) Do you have any other questions or concerns?

steps.title: Objection: Sensitivity or a bad experience before
steps.content:
I completely understand, and that's exactly the kind of thing {{rec_pronoun}}'ll want to talk through in person, so {{rec_pronoun}} can look at the whole picture and make it comfortable. (Never give dental advice on the call.)

Confirm and continue: Does that make sense? (Wait for a fast yes.) Do you have any other questions or concerns?

steps.title: Objection: I need to think about it
steps.content:
That's completely fair, {{contact_first_name}}. Can I ask what part you'd want to think over? Sometimes it's the cost, sometimes the timing, and sometimes people just want to be sure it's right for them, which one is closest for you?

(Listen, their answer usually points to one of the other buttons below. If it stays general, keep going.)

The nice thing is, coming in is really just information. You'd get a look at what's possible and exactly what it would involve, and then you get to decide with real answers instead of wondering. No pressure either way.

Confirm and continue: Does that make sense? (Wait for a fast yes.) Do you have any other questions or concerns?

steps.title: Objection: Just send me information
steps.content:
I'd be glad to get you some information, {{contact_first_name}}. The one thing I'd say is that a link or a flyer can only tell you so much. It can't really show you what's possible for you specifically. That's what a quick visit is for: you get a look at your options and answers that actually apply to you. So let me get you on the schedule first, no pressure, and you'll have real answers to go on.

Confirm and continue: Does that make sense? (Wait for a fast yes.) Do you have any other questions or concerns?
